items.title: Mayor Dorothy McCabe – Opposition to the Consolidation of
notes: Motion tabled February 9, 2026 for Council consideration February 23, 2026.

WHEREAS the Conservation Authorities Act, 1990 (the “Act”), originally enacted in 1946, was established to allow municipalities to form conservation authorities equipped to deliver local, watershed-based conservation, restoration, and natural resource management programs on behalf of both the province and municipalities; and,
WHEREAS Ontario’s thirty-six (36) conservation authorities are each distinct, reflecting the unique environmental, geographic, and community needs of their respective watersheds; and,
WHEREAS municipalities have long relied on their conservation authorities to tailor programs to local watershed priorities while ensuring fair and transparent costs for ratepayers; and,

WHEREAS municipalities are best positioned to understand the needs of their local communities and environments, and the existing watershed- based structure enables effective, collaborative approaches to water conservation and resource management that cannot be replicated through centralized oversight; and,

WHEREAS Bill 68 (Schedule 3) and ERO Posting 025-1257 propose consolidating Ontario’s 36 conservation authorities into seven regional authorities and creating the Ontario Provincial Conservation Agency, a Crown agency that would assume oversight and possess the authority to levy conservation authorities for its costs; and,

THAT the City of Waterloo formally state that it opposes the consolidation of Ontario’s conservation authorities without knowing the full financial and operational impact to municipalities and the conservation authorities; and, THAT the City of Waterloo require that the province meaningfully consult with municipalities prior to advancing any changes that could affect local control and management of the floodplain areas watersheds and natural resources which Conservation Authorities were established to manage;

AND THAT a copy of this motion be forwarded to The Honourable Doug Ford, Premier of Ontario; The Honourable Todd McCarthy, Minister of Environment, Conservation and Parks; local and area MPPs; the Grand River Conservation Authority (GRCA); the Association of Municipalities of Ontario (AMO); the Association of Municipal Managers, Clerks and Treasurers of Ontario (AMCTO); and to the Region of Waterloo and local area municipalities.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Hanmer gave a shoutout to Ward 1, the place to be yesterday February 8, as the Beachwood Homes Associations got together to host their annual Beechwood Winterfest. There were approximately 200-250 people that braved the cold. She offered a shoutout to the organizers and a thank you to the Neighbourhoods team that provided rentals and grants.

Councillor Hanmer also mentioned the Westvale Neighbourhood Association had their annual skate at Albert McCormick Community Centre. There were a lot of people out for that, and they also had an information session and discussion on climate action, trying to get a neighbourhood movement behind new initiatives.
Councillor Roe attended the Sanguen Health Centre’s Share the Love event last week, February 4, at the Victoria Park Pavilion. It was an incredible event with a great turnout.
Sanguen had their vehicles to tour, including their medical bus. It was an eye opener to see the support they offer the marginalized members of the community.
Councillor Roe also offered her thanks to Commissioner Ron Ormson and the transportation team for the work they’re doing this Winter and the challenges they’re facing.

Councillor Vasic mentioned that the Senior of the Year program is open again to nominate an exceptional senior in Waterloo. Nominations are open until March 31, and everyone who is nominated will be recognized.
Councillor Wright mentioned that Council for a day is coming up on April 16.

Councillor Roe also wanted to mention that Schlegel Village at University Gates is hosting their Olympics this Thursday, February 12 starting at 10am. All of the different Schlegel Village retirement homes are bringing in their athletes and it should be a lot of fun.

Councillor Roach had the opportunity to represent Waterloo this past Wednesday, February 4 in Ottawa to celebrate 30 years of Black History Month in Canada. He got to meet some great people, including Mark Carney, Marc Miller, and Greg Fergus who were all interested in the events happening in Waterloo. Mayor McCabe and Councillor Roach had attended an event a few days prior at the University of Waterloo, and Councillor Roach was able to share the entrepreneurial events he learned about there with the other representatives in Ottawa.

Mayor McCabe expanded on the information provided by Councillor Roach about the event at the University of Waterloo, held by BRIDGE (Black Regional Innovation Dialogue and Growth Exchange) with the Caribbean community and the University of Waterloo Engineering Society on January 30. It was a fascinating discussion, including topics such as culturally adept AI, and entrepreneurship.
Mayor McCabe also offered thanks to snow clearing crews, for their work with the historic snowfalls and in extreme temperatures this challenging winter.

Mayor McCabe also expanded on Council for a Day, and encouraged grade 5 students to submit their ideas. Eight lucky students will get to attend the State of the City on April 16, and spend the day with Council touring different facilities at the City. There is more information on waterloo.ca.
Mayor McCabe highlighted that the Olympics have started, and extended her best wishes to all the athletes competing for Canada.

motions.item_title: Mayor Dorothy McCabe – Resolution Regarding Legislative Changes
motions.text: WHEREAS the Ontario Municipal Employees Retirement System (OMERS) Pension Fund serves over 1,000 employers and over half a million employees and retirees from diverse groups including: municipal governments, school boards, libraries, police and fire departments, children’s aid societies, and electricity distribution companies; and, WHEREAS the long-standing jointly-sponsored governance model with two corporate boards has provided stability, accountability, and fairness for both plan members and employers for more than two decades; and, WHEREAS the Government of Ontario has passed legislative changes to OMERS’ governance structure through Bill 68; and, WHEREAS these changes would replace the current OMERS Sponsors Corporation with a new Sponsors Council that would lose its corporate status and independent resources; and, WHEREAS the proposed model could allow pension decisions affecting municipal employers and employees to be made without meaningful municipal oversight, increasing financial risk for municipalities and local taxpayers; and, WHEREAS municipalities are already under significant financial strain and cannot absorb additional pension costs without consequences for property taxes or local services; NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED: THAT the City of Waterloo does not support the legislative changes to the OMERS Act contained in Bill 68 and requests that the Government of Ontario reconsider the advisability of proceeding with these changes; and, THAT the City of Waterloo Council supports the Association of Municipalities of Ontario (AMO) in calling on the Government of Ontario to maintain the current OMERS governance model, with two corporate Boards, as the structure that would best deliver on the long-term interests of municipalities, taxpayers, and employees; AND THAT a copy of this motion be forwarded to The Honourable Doug Ford, Premier of Ontario; The Honourable Rob Flack, Minister of Housing and Municipal Affairs; The Honourable Peter Bethlenfalvy, Minister of Finance; local and area MPPs; the Association of Municipalities of Ontario (AMO); the Association of Municipal Managers, Clerks and Treasurers of Ontario (AMCTO); and to the Region of Waterloo and local area municipalities.
